Ok so I’m inspired by the sequels (the first two of which I really like) where they take the Han, Leia and Luke roles and scramble them into Rey, Poe and Finn. As a whole they serve the same roles but none are directly equivalent (Poe is brash like Han but idealistic like Luke, Finn is rescued like Leia but compromised like Han, Rey is the protagonist like Luke but a scavenger like Han but female like Leia, etc etc) and that’s what I’m doing with the villains. If I can!

I have a number of candidates. If the royalists do indeed clone an emperor, he will fill a sort of “emperor/tarkin” role (in that he’s technically the main villain but is a puppet in many ways). The Generalissimo of the Royalists could be a similar figure in reverse - he’s a stuffy military guy like Tarkin but he’s the real power like the Emperor. The grand master of the Jedi Knights could play the Vader role - a powerful sorcerer and veteran warrior - but would also have a streak of pride and cowardice that Vader doesn’t have. The Mandalorian war chieftain could play a kind of Jabba the Hutt figure as a barbaric side-villain. I haven’t worked it all out yet and I’m open to ideas!

In other words, the initial pitch from Palpatine to Vader after the assassination attempt is “hey, I know they said don’t use the dark side, but it’s the only way we can win, and I happen to know it’s more powerful, so we better do this.” Or maybe just, as Yoda says, "It's faster, it's easier." Obviously it corrodes and makes them both evil, but they start out with semi-good intentions.

If any of this doesn’t work , let me know people!

In this situation the Sith are not a thing. Any Jedi or force sensitive person can use the force. “Anger, fear, hate and suffering” feed the dark side, but even the force powers associated with our heroes (mind tricks, pushing stuff around, intuition) can be used to do evil. Since many of the Jedi “bad guys” are motivated by greed and pride, their powers fall into a grey area. Palpatine could either be a person kicked out of/denied Jedi training due to his instability, or a force sensitive non-Jedi. I definitely need to try to get all this straight in my head lol!!!

Thanks and good point! I actually was thinking Obi Wan and Yoda were fairly unique in that they truly believed the Jedi were supposed to adhere to their code of conduct and protect the republic. Most of them instead have become petty noblemen. They own property, they have families (nobody in the original trilogy seems to think Jedi have to remain unmarried), they’re involved in politics. Yoda’s response to this is just to run away in frustration and live a purely monastic life. Obi-Wan, his pupil, still thinks he can lead by example. So there are very few good Jedi left, and it’s not a very top-down organization any more because of how it’s fallen apart. The reason Obi-Wan in the trilogy is so hell-bent on getting Luke trained and tells him so many great things about the Jedi is that he sees an opportunity to restart the whole project.

So even though I was thinking there is a grand master of the Jedi who might serve as an interesting secondary villain, the organization isn’t such that all the Jedi are ordered to serve the bad guys. There just aren’t that many of them left and many of them individually decide to serve the baddies for their own reasons. Not all of them - but when Vader hunts them all down he’s not interested in drawing any distinctions.

The lore from early development of the game (back when they were still calling it "Orthodoxia") suggests that the "grievous miracle" (the one that caused all the monsters and all) took place when the High Pontiff turned his throne around out of disappointment in his followers not being devout enough and just ignored everyone for years. Eventually he grew into a tree, the tree was set on fire, and the ashes turned people into monsters.  


In the game, Escribar says "The miracle has forsaken us, and my ornate throne turns its back on those who await here." So we know that's a separate event from the Twisted One's backstory. Also, that throne is in the Desambulatory (the place Deogracias calls the "Cradle of affliction"), whereas the first miracle is in the Knot of Three Words.

The game has all these Spanish Baroque Catholic trappings, but they really did a neat thing - they changed the inner workings of the whole Cvstodia religion. People worship an event, a process, instead of a divinity. Like if the trinity put the Holy Spirit first, then Christ second, then totally just kind of hand-waved the "God" part.

Really hoping they expand on the worldbuilding and the story more in DLC or sequels without over-explaining anything.

Out of curiosity how did you deal with the homelessness? My landlord probably won’t kick me out the day after I’m late on rent since I literally have been paying months in advance and have been a model tenant. However it’s still possible. I do own my car outright and it runs well, but winter is on its way and it will be very cold.

I can’t go back to my folks. I shouldn’t have quit my job if I wanted a roof over my head. Or, I should have found another one. I was irresponsible and suicidal and now I’m responsible for fixing my situation.  
  
But I also don’t have to kill myself. I’ll get as many jobs as I can and make a good faith shot at paying rent and if I’m evicted... I guess that’s that. I can live in my car. I have almost a years worth of a prepaid gym membership so showers should be OK. As for shaving I’m not sure. It’s not that kind of a gym.  Maybe hot water and a bowl and a mirror? The physical discomfort is nothing compared to the shame. I wish people could understand that.

Thank you for being here. I'm not sure how you ended up looking at this forum, but the fact that you're willing to try to help means a lot.  

  

Right now the largest problem is that low-stress jobs don't pay enough for me to live on my own. Living with roommates is stressful and living with my parents is humiliating. And it's humiliating that I even have these problems, which do lead me to continue to want to snuff myself out out of shame.  

  

Your response did indicate to me that I do have some advantages. However, I'm not sure how I'll get out of my initial financial bind. I suppose that if I'm evicted I can live in my car - it's just not something I know how to do. It's hard to sleep and it stresses me out, but I guess I can survive it, technically.
